amendment_history.note: الإصدار الأصلي والوحيد المُثبت نصه في هذا المسار (24 مادة، أربعة أبواب) -- تصديقًا على نظام هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد بموجب قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (68) وتاريخ 17/1/1446هـ. بحسب صفحة هيئة الخبراء (Wayback Machine، لقطتان بينهما نحو 15.5 شهرًا: 1 نوفمبر 2024 و15 فبراير 2026، ومطابقة إضافية عبر نسخة PDF من FAOLEX مؤرخة 16 يونيو 2025)، لم يطرأ أي تعديل على مستوى المادة حتى الآن (24 مادة، جميعها بحالة 'اصلية'، دون أي علامة 'مادة معدلة' على الصفحة). يحل محل تنظيم الهيئة الوطنية لمكافحة الفساد الصادر بقرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (165) وتاريخ 28/5/1432هـ، ويلغي نظام تأديب الموظفين الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/7) وتاريخ 1/2/1391هـ (مع استثناء المادة 47 منه)، ويستبدل عبارة 'هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد' بعبارة 'رئاسة أمن الدولة' أينما وردت في نظام مكافحة الرشوة الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/36) وتاريخ 29/12/1412هـ (انظر known_unresolved_discrepancies، المفتاح nazaha_anti_bribery_crossref_articles_17_21_stale).

verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: laws.boe.gov.sa's LIVE portal was unreachable this pass for this law (direct HTTPS request to the exact law-detail URL [https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/a8ebff8e-412c-4f67-ac5f-b1ca008d18d9/1] returned no response / curl exit code 000), consistent with this corpus's established pattern for this BOE portal. archive.org/wayback/available confirmed TWO separate Wayback Machine snapshots of this exact BOE law-detail page roughly 15.5 months apart -- 20241101220240 (1 Nov 2024, HTTP 200, 74160 bytes) and 20260215014056 (15 Feb 2026, HTTP 200, 92130 bytes) -- both were fetched and parsed with BeautifulSoup (not naive regex/tag-stripping): each of 24 'article_item' divs carries an 'h3.center' heading (a bare ordinal, e.g. 'المادة الأولى', with NO inline topic title after it) and a 'div.HTMLContainer' body; four باب (chapter/part) headings ('h3.center' elements whose text begins with 'الباب') interleave with the article headings in document order, giving an unambiguous chapter-to-article mapping. CRITICALLY, all 24 'article_item' divs in BOTH snapshots carry ONLY the class 'no_alternate' (BOE's no-op/default marker) -- zero occurrences of any 'changed-article' or amended/repealed marker class anywhere on either snapshot -- and a byte-for-byte comparison of the extracted text of all 24 articles between the two snapshots found ZERO differences. This is strong, direct evidence that the law remains wholly unamended at the article level as of the most recent available snapshot. A THIRD, INDEPENDENT TIME-POINT: a PDF hosted by FAOLEX (FAO's legal database, faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/sau236079.pdf, fetched live this pass, 308509 bytes, 8 pages) is itself a saved browser printout of this exact same BOE URL, dated 16/06/2025 (per the printout's own header 'تاريخ الطباعة: 1446/12/20هـ الموافق 16/06/2025م' and footer URL 'https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/a8ebff8e-412c-4f67-ac5f-b1ca008d18d9/1'). Extracted via pdftotext -layout, its article text (spot-checked in full for Articles 19-24 and the الباب الرابع heading) matches the two Wayback snapshots verbatim. This gives three independent time-points (1 Nov 2024, 16 Jun 2025, 15 Feb 2026) spanning roughly 15.5 months, all showing byte/word-identical, wholly unamended text -- a materially stronger verification tier than this corpus's typical single-Wayback-snapshot fallback. SECONDARY CROSS-VERIFICATION (independent domains, partial + structural): (1) nezams.com (a Saudi legal-publishing aggregator, fetched live this pass) independently confirms the same decree number/dates (م/25, 23/1/1446H; CoM Resolution 68, 17/1/1446H; publication 5/2/1446H), the same status ('ساري'), and explicitly states 'لم يجرِ عليه تعديل' (no amendment has been made to it) -- and its fetched excerpt's verbatim text for Articles 1-14 (topically summarized by the fetch tool) matches BOE's text in substance for every article checked. This did not yield the full 24-article verbatim text in one fetch, so it is treated as a PARTIAL, not full-text, cross-check for Articles 15-24, consistent with this corpus's stated 1-2-verification-attempts-per-fact policy. (2) qanoonsa.com (fetched live this pass) independently corroborates the exact same four-باب structure and article ranges (تعريفات 1-2؛ جهاز الهيئة ومهماته واختصاصاته 3-17؛ أحكام متصلة بمكافحة جرائم الفساد 18-22؛ أحكام ختامية 23-24) and the same total article count (24) and decree/gazette details (Umm Al-Qura Gazette Issue 5042, 9 Aug 2024). STATUS FIELD PROGRESSION (informational, not a discrepancy): the 1 Nov 2024 snapshot's 'الحالة' (status) metadata field read 'ساري خلال مدة' (in force, within [a grace] period) -- i.e. published but the 90-day period before full effect specified in this law's own Article 24 had not yet elapsed (publication 9 Aug 2024 + 90 days ≈ 7 Nov 2024, i.e. six days after this snapshot). By the 15 Feb 2026 snapshot, the status field reads plain 'ساري' (in force). Both readings are consistent with each other and with Article 24's own text; this is the law's expected vacatio-legis lifecycle, not a source disagreement. REPEAL / SUPERSESSION CLAUSES -- CONFIRMED, EXPLICIT, MULTI-INSTRUMENT: unlike a simple single-predecessor repeal, this law's own enacting instruments (read in full from BOE, both the Royal Decree M/25 text and the Council of Ministers Resolution 68 text, which are textually near-identical and both fully extracted this pass) contain SIX explicit repeal/consequential-amendment clauses, none of them ingested as this track's own articles (this track ingests only the 24-article نظام text itself), but all documented here as critical context: (a) clause سادساً/'سادساً' repeals نظام تأديب الموظفين (the general Civil Service Disciplinary Law, Royal Decree M/7, 1/2/1391H) effective from this law's own enforcement date, EXCEPT that its Article 47 remains in force until the new اللائحة الإدارية under this law's own Article 9(1) is issued; (b) clause سابعاً replaces the phrase 'رئاسة أمن الدولة' (State Security Presidency) with 'هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد' wherever it appears in نظام مكافحة الرشوة (the Anti-Bribery Law, Royal Decree M/36, 29/12/1412H -- this corpus's already-ingested anti_bribery_law track; see nazaha_anti_bribery_crossref_articles_17_21_stale below); (c) clause ثامناً replaces the phrases 'الهيئة الوطنية لمكافحة الفساد' / 'هيئة الرقابة والتحقيق' / 'المباحث الإدارية' (and their 'رئيس' equivalents) with 'هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد' / 'رئيس هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد' wherever they appear in ANY law/regulation/order/decree/resolution -- this is the clause that confirms, in BOE's own primary text, the three predecessor-body names being consolidated (see PREDECESSOR HISTORY below); (d) clause تاسعاً (CoM Resolution numbering; ninth item after 'ثامناً' in the decree text, following an intervening 'وقد أعد مشروع مرسوم ملكي...' sentence) explicitly repeals تنظيم الهيئة الوطنية لمكافحة الفساد (the predecessor National Anti-Corruption Commission's own organizational statute, Council of Ministers Resolution No. 165, 28/5/1432H) effective from this law's own enforcement date; (e) clause عاشراً keeps the predecessor commission's old financial/administrative regulations in force until this Authority's own new ones (per Article 9(1)) are issued; (f) Article 23 of the law itself (in الباب الرابع) additionally states, in general terms, 'يُلغي هذا النظام كل ما يتعارض معه من أحكام أخرى' (this Law repeals whatever conflicts with it). PREDECESSOR HISTORY (background/context only -- NOT ingested as articles, per this corpus's standard practice for confirmed supersessions): this present-day Authority (هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد) traces to three distinct predecessor/merged bodies, per multiply-corroborated secondary sources plus BOE's own primary consequential-amendment text (clause ثامناً, above): (1) الهيئة الوطنية لمكافحة الفساد (National Anti-Corruption Commission), established by Royal Order No. (أ/65) dated 13/4/1432H (18 March 2011G) -- its own organizational statute (تنظيم) was issued the same year by Council of Ministers Resolution No. (165) dated 28/5/1432H (this exact CoM-Resolution-165 citation is independently corroborated from TWO directions: secondary web sources reporting the 2011 founding, AND BOE's own primary repeal clause تاسعاً in the 2024 decree, which cites this same instrument number/date as the one being repealed -- a strong internal-consistency check even though this pass did not fetch a live/current BOE snapshot showing this predecessor's status flipped to لاغي; see nazaha_predecessor_boe_status_lag below); (2) هيئة الرقابة والتحقيق (the Control and Investigation Board, a pre-existing separate body, exact founding instrument not independently re-verified this pass -- out of scope, historical only); (3) المباحث الإدارية (Administrative Investigation, a pre-existing separate body, exact founding instrument not independently re-verified this pass -- out of scope, historical only). Bodies (2) and (3) were merged INTO body (1) by a further Royal Order No. (أ/277) dated 15/4/1441H (approx. 12 December 2019G per multiple secondary press sources: okaz.com.sa, al-jazirah.com, my.gov.sa, saudipedia.com), at which point the merged entity was renamed هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد -- this exact number/date is independently corroborated by BOE's OWN 2024 Council of Ministers Resolution 68 preamble, which cites 'الترتيبات التنظيمية والهيكلية المتصلة بمكافحة الفساد المالي والإداري، الموافق عليها بالأمر الملكي رقم (أ/277) وتاريخ 15/4/1441هـ' as a recital. This present nظام (M/25, 23/1/1446H) is thus NOT an amendment of any of these three predecessor instruments -- it is a wholesale replacement organizing statute for the already-merged/renamed Authority, adopted roughly five years after the 2019 merger. Neither predecessor instrument's own full article text is ingested in this track; only this present, current, 24-article نظام is ingested. STRUCTURE: this Law IS subdivided into four أبواب (parts), each with its own BOE-sourced h3-level title, confirmed identically across both BOE Wayback snapshots and independently corroborated by qanoonsa.com's structural summary: الباب الأول (تعريفات, Arts. 1-2), الباب الثاني (جهاز الهيئة ومهماته واختصاصاته, Arts. 3-17), الباب الثالث (أحكام متصلة بمكافحة جرائم الفساد, Arts. 18-22), الباب الرابع (أحكام ختامية, Arts. 23-24). No فصول (chapter) subdivision exists within any باب. No individual article carries an inline topic title (every 'h3.center' heading for an article is a bare ordinal, e.g. 'المادة الأولى', with nothing following it) -- consistent with this corpus's accounting_auditing_law precedent for BOE sources lacking inline per-article titles, no title_ar field is used; section_ar instead carries each article's باب title for structural/topical context. IMPLEMENTING/COMPANION INSTRUMENTS: this law's own text references three forthcoming subordinate instruments, none confirmed issued as of this pass (18 Jul 2026): (a) Article 6 references a لائحة (to be drafted by the Authority and submitted to the King) governing how Criminal Procedure Law and Public Prosecution Law provisions apply to corruption crimes; (b)-(c) Article 9(1) references a forthcoming اللائحة الإدارية (Administrative Regulation, covering inter alia staff discipline rules, explicitly excluding military personnel and Unit members) and a forthcoming اللائحة المالية (Financial Regulation), both also to be submitted to the King. The enacting Council of Ministers Resolution's own clause عاشراً confirms neither the Administrative nor Financial Regulation had been issued as of enactment (it keeps the PREDECESSOR commission's old financial/administrative regulations in force in the interim). Targeted web searches this pass found no confirmation that any of these three companion instruments have since been issued/published under the renamed Authority. Per this corpus's established precedent (finance_lease_law, banking_control_law, insurance_control_law, accounting_auditing_law, gcc_anti_dumping_law, and others), this track ingests ONLY the primary organizing statute (24 articles); none of these three forthcoming/unconfirmed companion regulations are ingested, fabricated, or guessed at. DISTINCTION FROM THIS CORPUS'S ALREADY-INGESTED anti_bribery_law TRACK: this track's law (نظام هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد, M/25, 23/1/1446H) is Nazaha's own ORGANIZING/ESTABLISHING statute -- its mandate, structure (chair at ministerial rank + deputy + assistant(s)), specialized units, the separate quasi-judicial Investigation and Criminal Prosecution Unit (وحدة التحقيق والادعاء الجنائي) and its Council, budget, reporting lines, and a handful of corruption-specific administrative/civil consequences (mandatory dismissal on conviction, reversed burden of proof for unexplained wealth, asset recovery, discretionary dismissal for integrity concerns, financial settlements). It is textually and substantively DISTINCT from نظام مكافحة الرشوة (the Anti-Bribery Law, Royal Decree M/36, 29/12/1412H), this corpus's already-ingested anti_bribery_law track, which defines and criminalizes the SUBSTANTIVE OFFENSE of bribery (who is a مرتشٍ/راشٍ, penalties, aggravating factors) -- this track does not re-ingest or restate any of the Anti-Bribery Law's offense-defining articles. The two instruments ARE textually linked at one point: this law's own enacting Royal Decree (clause سابعاً) directly amends the Anti-Bribery Law by substituting 'هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد' for 'رئاسة أمن الدولة' wherever the latter phrase appears in it -- see nazaha_anti_bribery_crossref_articles_17_21_stale below for a significant, currently-unresolved cross-track finding this substitution surfaced. No legal text is altered beyond whitespace/line-break normalization needed to render BOE's HTML as plain text (converting literal
tags to newlines; joining inline / runs within the same
  • /

    without an inserted separator, so that e.g. a lettered sub-item's 'أ-' label and its following text remain on one line, matching how they visually render on the source page; treating each

  • /

    as starting a new line). Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation performed on the Arabic text (English descriptions in this note and in document_en/issuing_authority_en are for indexing only). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: CRITICAL CROSS-TRACK FINDING (this track's single most important documented discrepancy). This law's own enacting Royal Decree text (clause سابعاً, read in full from BOE this pass) explicitly states: 'إحلال عبارة "هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد" محل عبارة "رئاسة أمن الدولة" أينما وردت في نظام مكافحة الرشوة، الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/36) وتاريخ 29/12/1412هـ' -- i.e. it directly amends this corpus's ALREADY-INGESTED anti_bribery_law track by substituting 'هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد' for 'رئاسة أمن الدولة' wherever the latter phrase appears in the Anti-Bribery Law, effective from this law's own enforcement date (~7 Nov 2024, 90 days after its 9 Aug 2024 gazette publication). However, sources/anti_bribery/law/official_source/anti_bribery_law_official_source.json's own known_unresolved_discrepancies (key anti_bribery_art_017) records that BOTH of its two secondary sources checked in that track's own build pass (manielaw-sa.com and nezams.com) still showed 'رئاسة أمن الدولة' in Articles 17 AND 21 of the Anti-Bribery Law, not 'هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد' -- meaning that track's currently-ingested text for Articles 17 and 21 no longer matches the current wording required by this law's own primary-source-verified consequential-amendment clause (a cross-track finding about anti_bribery_law's own source currency, not about this nazaha_law track's own primary source, which remains independently verified as current). (Separately, that same anti_bribery_law track's own Article 14 record already carries the UPDATED 'هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد' wording, which its own note attributes to 'the 2024 Royal Decree M/25... rename of the national anti-corruption authority' -- a mostly-correct but imprecise attribution: M/25 did not itself rename the Authority [it was already renamed by the 2019 Royal Order أ/277, see PREDECESSOR HISTORY in this track's verification_methodology_note]; M/25 is instead the instrument whose clause ثامناً directs this exact terminology substitution across all other Saudi legal instruments, including, via its distinct clause سابعاً, the Anti-Bribery Law specifically.) This nazaha track does NOT itself modify, re-fetch, or re-verify anti_bribery_law's files (out of scope for this build pass, per instructions restricting this pass to this track's own four file-groups only) -- this finding is flagged explicitly here, and reported to the requester, for a dedicated follow-up pass to re-verify and, if confirmed, correct anti_bribery_law's Articles 17 and 21 (updating 'رئاسة أمن الدولة' to 'هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد' and adding a corresponding amendment_history entry citing Royal Decree M/25, 23/1/1446H, clause سابعاً).

This present-day Authority traces to الهيئة الوطنية لمكافحة الفساد (National Anti-Corruption Commission), established by Royal Order No. (أ/65) dated 13/4/1432H (18 March 2011G) -- a number/date corroborated by this corpus's own coverage_gap_map.json entry for this law ('Royal Order No. 65/A dated 13/4/1432H') and by multiple secondary web sources consulted this pass (a WebSearch AI synthesis citing several Saudi press outlets, and saudipedia.com's own establishment-date entry, '2011م' / '13 ربيع الآخر 1432هـ'). This is further corroborated indirectly and internally: BOE's own 2024 repeal clause (تاسعاً in the Royal Decree text) cites Council of Ministers Resolution No. (165) dated 28/5/1432H -- the SAME hijri year, and the organizational-statute instrument that would naturally follow a same-year founding order -- as the predecessor commission's own organizational statute being repealed. However, this pass did NOT independently fetch or read Royal Order أ/65's own primary gazette text (only its number/date, via secondary sources) -- it is documented here purely as confirmed historical/background context (NOT ingested as articles), consistent with this corpus's practice for confirmed predecessor supersessions, and its exact number should be treated as well-attested-but-not-primary-source-verified.

On 15/4/1441H (approx. 12 December 2019G), Royal Order No. (أ/277) merged هيئة الرقابة والتحقيق (the Control and Investigation Board) and المباحث الإدارية (Administrative Investigation) into الهيئة الوطنية لمكافحة الفساد (the National Anti-Corruption Commission), renaming the combined entity هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد (the present-day Authority's current name). This exact number/date is corroborated from TWO independent directions: (a) multiple secondary Saudi press sources (okaz.com.sa, al-jazirah.com, my.gov.sa/news/8222, saudipedia.com), all citing 12 December 2019 for this merger; and (b) BOE's OWN primary text for this present law's enacting Council of Ministers Resolution 68 (fetched and read in full this pass), whose preamble cites 'الترتيبات التنظيمية والهيكلية المتصلة بمكافحة الفساد المالي والإداري، الموافق عليها بالأمر الملكي رقم (أ/277) وتاريخ 15/4/1441هـ' as a recital -- an exact number/date match with the secondary press reports. Royal Order أ/277's own full primary gazette text was NOT independently fetched/read this pass (only its number/date/effect, via BOE's own recital plus secondary sources) -- it is documented here as confirmed historical/background context only (NOT ingested as articles), per this corpus's standard practice.

The predecessor commission's own BOE-catalogued organizational statute page (تنظيم الهيئة الوطنية لمكافحة الفساد, lawId 7d36fabe-eabc-42b0-a536-a9a700f2d66f, Council of Ministers Resolution No. 165, 28/5/1432H) was fetched via its only available Wayback Machine snapshot (20241012153629, 12 Oct 2024) and its status field still read 'ساري' (in force) at that time -- NOT yet 'لاغي' (repealed/void), even though this present law's own enacting decree (clause تاسعاً) repeals that exact instrument. This is fully consistent, not contradictory: the repeal is stated to take effect 'اعتبارًا من تاريخ نفاذ النظام' (from the date this present law itself enters into force), which per this law's own Article 24 is 90 days after its 9 Aug 2024 gazette publication -- i.e. approximately 7 Nov 2024, about a month AFTER the 12 Oct 2024 snapshot. No later Wayback snapshot of the predecessor's BOE page exists (CDX query for this exact URL returned only the single 12 Oct 2024 snapshot), so this pass could not directly confirm BOE has since flipped that page's status field to لاغي; this is a plausible, expected timing gap given the confirmed repeal clause, not an unresolved conflict over whether the repeal itself is real.

This corpus's own reports/coverage_gap_map/coverage_gap_map.json entry for this law described the estimated governing instrument as 'Established by Royal Order No. 65/A dated 13/4/1432H (2011); the Authority's organizational system/statute governs its investigative and disciplinary powers' and left 'estimated_article_count: Not confirmed — needs verification'. This pass's direct BOE verification corrects and updates this: Royal Order أ/65 (13/4/1432H) founded a PREDECESSOR body (الهيئة الوطنية لمكافحة الفساد), whose own 2011 organizational statute (Council of Ministers Resolution 165, 28/5/1432H) was a materially DIFFERENT, now-repealed instrument. The CURRENT governing organizing statute for the present-day هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد (renamed via a further 2019 merger order, أ/277) is Royal Decree No. (م/25) dated 23/1/1446H (29 July 2024G), based on Council of Ministers Resolution No. (68) dated 17/1/1446H -- a wholesale replacement statute, not an amendment of the 2011/2019 instruments -- confirmed to contain exactly 24 articles, organized into four أبواب.

This law's BOE-hosted HTML supplies NO inline title text for any of its 24 articles -- every 'h3.center' heading for an article is a bare ordinal (e.g. 'المادة الأولى') with nothing following it, across both Wayback snapshots checked. Consistent with this corpus's accounting_auditing_law precedent for BOE sources lacking inline per-article titles, no title_ar key is used for any article; section_ar instead carries each article's باب (chapter/part) title for structural/topical context, since -- unlike accounting_auditing_law -- this law IS subdivided into four named أبواب.

This law's own text references THREE forthcoming subordinate instruments, none confirmed issued as of this pass (18 Jul 2026): (a) Article 6's لائحة governing how Criminal Procedure Law/Public Prosecution Law provisions apply to corruption crimes; (b) Article 9(1)'s forthcoming اللائحة الإدارية (Administrative Regulation, covering staff discipline rules, excluding military personnel and Unit members); (c) Article 9(1)'s forthcoming اللائحة المالية (Financial Regulation). The enacting Council of Ministers Resolution's own clause عاشراً confirms neither the Administrative nor Financial Regulation had been issued as of enactment (predecessor regulations were kept in force in the interim). Targeted web searches this pass found no confirmation any of the three have since been issued/published under the renamed Authority's name. Per this corpus's established precedent, this track ingests ONLY the primary organizing statute (24 articles); none of these three forthcoming/unconfirmed companion instruments are ingested, fabricated, or guessed at.

This track's law (نظام هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد, Royal Decree M/25, 23/1/1446H) is Nazaha's own ORGANIZING/ESTABLISHING statute -- mandate, structure, units, the quasi-judicial Investigation and Criminal Prosecution Unit and its Council, budget, reporting, and a handful of corruption-specific administrative/civil consequences. It is textually and substantively DISTINCT from نظام مكافحة الرشوة (the Anti-Bribery Law, Royal Decree M/36, 29/12/1412H), this corpus's already-ingested anti_bribery_law track, which defines and criminalizes the substantive offense of bribery. This track does not re-ingest or restate any of the Anti-Bribery Law's offense-defining articles. The two instruments are textually linked at exactly one point -- this law's own enacting Royal Decree (clause سابعاً) amends the Anti-Bribery Law by substituting 'هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد' for 'رئاسة أمن الدولة' wherever the latter appears in it -- see nazaha_anti_bribery_crossref_articles_17_21_stale above for a significant, currently-unresolved cross-track staleness finding this substitution surfaced in the already-ingested anti_bribery_law track's own Articles 17 and 21.
